Italian fascism ( Italian : fascismo italiano ), also called classical fascism or simply fascism , is the original fascist ideology, which Giovanni Gentile and Benito Mussolini developed in Italy. The ideology of Italian fascism is associated with a series of political parties led by Mussolini: the National Fascist Party (PNF), which governed the Kingdom of Italy from 1922 until 1943, [ 7 ] and the Republican Fascist Party (PFR), which governed the Italian Social Republic (RSI) from 1943 to 1945. [ 8 ] Italian fascism is also associated with the post-war Italian Social Movement (MSI) and later Italian neo-fascist political organizations . [ 9 ]
